history.period: Ancient (Mahavira era, 6th c. BCE); present structures 20th century
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE (Digambara sect), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Vaishali (Kundgram/Kundalpur) is held by the Digambara tradition to be the birthplace of Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, born c. 599 BCE as prince of the Licchavi republic of Vaishali. A Digambar source records that the presiding idol of Mahavira was recovered from Bauna lake south of the temple and is believed to be over 2,000 years old, and that older Jain temples here were demolished under the rule of Gayasuddin. The Vaishali Research Institute (for Prakrit and Jain studies) and the Mahavir Memorial were established in 1945, which revived the area's development. Coordinates are for the Vaishali archaeological site; exact temple coordinates UNVERIFIED.

name: Shri Digambar Jain Mandir, Vaishali
town_description: Vaishali is an ancient city in Vaishali district, Bihar, capital of the Licchavi clan's republic — often cited as one of the world's earliest republics (6th century BCE). It is a major pilgrimage centre for Jains (birthplace of Lord Mahavira) and Buddhists (Ashoka pillar, stupas, the Second Buddhist Council). The area is rich in archaeological remains and lies about 60 km north of Patna.
